name: M1 backend: Gmail account model, secure token storage and OAuth connect/disconnect API
description:
MILESTONE 1 (backend half) — a user can connect a real Gmail account and disconnect it. Deployable on its own; nothing waits for reading or sending.

Profiles chosen: py_senior (owns the Python model/API/security work) and software_developer (implements the endpoint wiring and integration).

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. GmailAccount pydantic model in api/codx/junior/model/user.py and a `gmail_accounts: List[GmailAccount]` field on CodxUser — follow the existing pattern of token_limit_rules.
2. api/codx/junior/security/google_oauth.py — a GoogleOAuth client modelled on the existing GitHubOAuth class (PKCE, state handling, authorization url, code->token exchange, token refresh).
3. Endpoints in api/codx/junior/api/users.py (scoped to the authenticated user only):
   - GET /users/me/gmail/accounts — list connected accounts (never expose refresh/access tokens)
   - GET /users/me/gmail/login-url — return the Google consent url
   - POST /users/me/gmail/callback — exchange code, store account, store refresh token encrypted
   - DELETE /users/me/gmail/accounts/{id} — revoke at Google and remove locally
4. Refresh-token storage must be encrypted at rest and never serialised into any API response or log.
5. Reuse get_oauth_provider("google") for client_id/secret so it works from settings or CODX_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / CODX_GOOGLE_SECRET.
6. Add the Google deps to api/pyproject.toml (google-auth / google-api-python-client or use direct HTTPS calls — state which and why).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- With a real Google OAuth client in Test/Internal mode, a logged-in user connects a Gmail account and it appears in GET /users/me/gmail/accounts with its address.
- The consent screen only asks for identity scopes in this milestone (no gmail.readonly yet) so M1 can deploy without triggering restricted-scope verification.
- Tokens never appear in response bodies or logs — verified by inspecting the payload.
- DELETE revokes the grant at Google and removes the local record.
- Existing user login and GitHub OAuth still work.
